title: How To Setup A Third Party Email Application To Access The Email Accounts | Brilliant Directories Documentation | BD Support
content: How To Setup A Third Party Email Application To Access The Email Accounts Link: https://support.brilliantdirectories.com/support/solutions/articles/12000003535 To set upTo setup a 3rd party email client (Outlook, Thunderbird, Macmail, Gmail, etc) to access the account, follow these steps to find out the proper settings to use: Navigate to Emails >> Email Accounts: Click on the " Add/Edit Email Addresses " button: Locate the email address to connect with the 3rd party email application and click on " Connect Devices ": Mail Client Configuration This section provides instructions on how to configure email connection settings. Automatic Connection Below is a collection of tutorials for configuring specific email applications. The appropriate protocol should be selected based on the email application in use. For Mac devices such as iPhone, iPad, or macOS, Mail.app, select the iOS option. For any Windows device, including those using Windows Live Mail, select the corresponding Windows option. Manual Connection Additionally, 'Manual Settings' are provided for configuring applications not included in the listed tutorials: Domain Connection Method It is necessary to identify the domain connection method being used to complete the email configuration. This information can be found in the Domain Manager. If the connection method is listed as 'NS', it indicates the use of nameservers. If it displays 'Cloudflare', 'CNAME', or any other value, the CNAME method is being used. Nameservers Domains If the site is connected via nameservers , the 'Incoming' and 'Outgoing' server details provided in the Secure SSL/TLS Settings table should be used: CNAME Domains If the domain was connected using a CNAME r ecord (meaning it is hosted with the domain registrar or Cloudflare, not with BD), and the 'Incoming Server' and 'Outgoing Server' details provided by cPanel are not working, use the secure target URL displayed in the Domain Manager as both the incoming and outgoing server address instead: Connection Example with IOS We will use the "Automatic Connection" for this example. Click on the IMAP over SSL/TLS option: Go to your device's "System Settings", and type "Email". Then select "Internet Accounts", and click on "Add Account": Select the "Mail Account" option: Since the domain is connected via a CNAME record, the 'Secure Target URL' displayed in the Domain Manager should be used as both the 'Incoming Mail Server' and the 'Outgoing Mail Server'. Refer to the 'Email Setup for CNAME Domains' section above for guidance. Add the email address and password. Then add the Incoming and Outgoing Mail Server. Select the applications that should be enabled for use with this account. Open the Mail application on the device; the email account will appear in the left sidebar.
